# Device CMYK JPEG color conversion diagnostic

Original 4-by-4 CMYK swatches and their simple RGB conversion, generated by
`tools/cmyk_jpeg_fixture.py`. No corpus artwork, ICC profile or external color
lookup table is included. The JPEGs are generated with Pillow; the package is
assembled with python-docx and original JPEG parts replace distinct placeholders.
Both image relationships must remain distinct.

The reference application exports `native.pdf`. `tools/record_cmyk_jpeg.py` records
source/PDF hashes, image frames, and 16 interior samples per picture. The native
page and browser page were visually inspected. The reference application converts unprofiled device
CMYK red (0,255,255,0) to (229,50,45), while the browser produces (255,0,0).
The RGB control agrees within one RGB level. This is consistent with the existing
TIFF CMYK gap, and does not establish any particular ICC conversion algorithm.

`tests/browser/cmyk-jpeg.spec.js` checks the RGB control normally and retains CMYK
color fidelity as an explicit expected failure. Frame/hash/import checks precede
the expected-failure marker. Color tolerances are not loosened to hide the gap.
Manual no-edit preservation, body editing, unrelated-part preservation, exact
undo and export/reopen pass. The control and three exports pass schema checks.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 15.2.14 and 20.1.8.13 allow image parts and reference
encoded pixels; these controls identify a reference color compatibility gap, not a
proven conflict with a prescribed OOXML conversion formula. No renderer change
or new dependency is included in this diagnostic.

## Exact native metafile palette (September 27, 2026)

`native-metafile.emf` is the reference application's first inline range, captured read-only
from this same original control. `native-metafile-reference.json` binds its hash
and the source hash. Its one EMR_STRETCHDIBITS record has a 256-by-128, bottom-up
8-bit uncompressed bitmap and an RGB palette. The sixteen recorded colors are
direct palette lookups at original swatch centers, without scaling, JPEG
recompression or PDF rasterization. The provenance unit test reconstructs them.
Capture again with `tools/capture-picture-metafile.ps1`, passing this source and
an output EMF path; inspect new evidence before replacing stored observations.

These colors differ from the PDF reference by up to three channel levels.
Direct Windows GDI+ decoding differs from the metafile by at most one level;
its color-management flag does not change any sampled pixel. Neither observation
establishes exact identity with the live reference application screen or every CMYK image.

The installed `RSWOP.icm` profile (Agfa Swop Standard) used privately with
LittleCMS is substantially closer than the browser's naive conversion, but
still differs from the PDF samples by up to five levels under perceptual intent.
Its identity and diagnostic samples are recorded; its vendor copyright notice is
recorded too. No profile binary or lookup table from it is bundled. Matching
the reference application still requires a portable conversion with acceptable provenance and
independent holdout controls, not a swatch-specific adjustment.

The new metafile browser oracle is an explicit expected failure. The older PDF
oracle and passing RGB control remain separate. This is better native evidence,
not a production decoder fix or a completed corpus review.
